title: Declining Profits at BlueBrew Coffee
prompt: Your client is BlueBrew, a chain of 40 campus coffee shops in the Northeast US. Over the last two years, revenue has been flat but profit has fallen by about 30%. The CEO wants to know why profits are declining and what to do about it. How would you approach this?
background: BlueBrew sells drinks (80% of revenue) and packaged food (20% of revenue).
All 40 stores are company-owned; none are franchised.
The chain has not raised drink prices in two years.
No new stores were opened or closed in the period.

clarifying_answers.What is the client's goal: Return profit to its level from two years ago within 12 months.
clarifying_answers.Has the product mix changed: Drinks vs. food split is unchanged at 80/20.
clarifying_answers.Is this an industry-wide trend: Competitors have raised prices ~8% over the same period; BlueBrew has not.
clarifying_answers.Revenue flat means: Total revenue is roughly 50 million dollars per year, unchanged.

exhibits.name: Cost Breakdown (annual, per year)
exhibits.description: Major cost lines two years ago vs. today.
exhibits.data: Two years ago: COGS 15M, Labor 12M, Rent 8M, Other 5M, total costs 40M on 50M revenue (profit 10M). Today: COGS 18M, Labor 15M, Rent 8M, Other 5M, total costs 46M on 50M revenue (profit ~7M, a ~30% drop).

exhibits.name: Unit Economics per Drink
exhibits.description: Average selling price and variable cost per drink.
exhibits.data: Average drink price $4.00 unchanged. Variable cost per drink rose from $1.20 to $1.55 (milk and coffee bean inflation). Volume ~10 million drinks/year, unchanged.

good_framework: Profit = Revenue - Costs; revenue is flat, so decompose costs.
Revenue side: price x volume, by product line (drinks vs. food); confirm neither is masking the other.
Cost side: split fixed (rent, salaried labor) vs. variable (COGS, hourly labor); find which line grew.
External: input-cost inflation, competitor pricing, wage pressure.
Tie back to the 12-month goal with concrete levers.

quant.question: By how much did total annual profit fall in dollars?
quant.work: Revenue 50M flat. Costs rose from 40M to 46M, so profit fell from 10M to ~7M, a ~3M / 30% drop.

quant.question: How much did rising variable cost per drink reduce annual profit?
quant.work: Variable cost per drink up $0.35 (1.55 - 1.20) x 10M drinks = $3.5M, which explains essentially all of the profit decline.

quant.question: If BlueBrew raised drink price by 8% (to ~$4.32), what is the annual revenue uplift at flat volume?
quant.work: $0.32 extra per drink x 10M drinks = $3.2M, roughly restoring lost profit if volume holds.

recommendation: The decline is almost entirely driven by input-cost inflation raising variable cost per drink by $0.35, cutting ~$3.5M of profit, while BlueBrew held price flat as competitors raised ~8%. Recommend a targeted price increase (~8%) plus supplier renegotiation on beans/milk; monitor volume elasticity. Risks: price-sensitive student segment and competitor response.
